## Kit

- King 1000/6000 combo stone, £38 from Nisbets, 2023
- Naniwa Chosera 3000, £62, the good one, bought March 2024
- Atoma 400 diamond plate for flattening, £55, worth every penny
- leather strop loaded with green compound
- Victorinox honing steel that lives on the truck, used every shift

Total so far £191, logged under "kit" in the [[Budget spreadsheet]]. The bloke at Altrincham market charges £8 a knife, I do 4 knives a week, so the stones paid for themselves in about 6 weeks.

## Angles

Tojiro DP F-808 gyuto, 210 mm: 15 degrees per side. Victorinox Fibrox 8 inch: 20 per side, the steel is soft and the edge rolls at 15. A matchbox under the spine gets you roughly 15 on the gyuto, two matchboxes for 20. Stop guessing, use the matchbox.

## Routine

1. Soak the King 10 min. The Chosera is splash-and-go, never soak it.
2. 1000 side until a burr runs the full length on one side, usually 30 strokes. Flip, same again.
3. Chosera 3000, half the pressure.
4. 6000 side, barely any pressure, alternating strokes.
5. 10 passes each side on the strop.

Test: it should slice a tomato skin under its own weight and shave arm hair. If it won't, back to the 1000.

## Schedule

Truck knives every Monday, about 25 min for 4. Flatten the stones every third session: pencil grid on the face, Atoma until the grid is gone. Same Monday I re-oil the pans, see [[Cast iron care]].

## Lessons

- pressure on the push stroke, light on the pull
- the Fibrox got a nick from a lamb bone in Feb 2025, took 40 min on the 1000 to grind it out
- never put the gyuto near the sink, Tash
- a properly sharp knife makes the prep for [[Weeknight stir fry]] twice as fast, I timed it: 11 min vs 19 min
